newsitem.title: JAPAN: Mitsuzuka did not say considering tax rise--MOF.
newsitem.headline: Mitsuzuka did not say considering tax rise--MOF.

text.p: Finance Minister Hiroshi Mitsuzuka did not say he was considering a further imminent rise in Japan's consumption tax, Vice Finance Minister Tadashi Ogawa told a news conference on Monday.
Ogawa was referring to a wire service report earlier in the day which quoted Mitsuzuka as saying he would not deny the possibility of a tax increase after the scheduled April 1 rise.
"(Mitsuzuka) has absolutely not said that he is considering (a further tax rise) with an imminent rise in the consumption tax in mind," Ogawa said.
Mitsuzuka was quoted by Jiji news agency as saying: "I would not deny a tax increase during the long course of managing the nation. Such a case is possible."
But Jiji quoted Mitsuzuka as saying that the possibility of an increase in the consumption tax could be considered only after discussions by a government advisory tax panel and the public.

The report triggered a selloff in Tokyo stocks, which in turn depressed the yen against the dollar. The benchmark Nikkei average of 225 leading shares ended down more than three percent on Monday at 589.34, mostly on Mitsuzuka's reported comments.
Ogawa said discussions over tax revenues, including the consumption tax, should be carried out each year after taking into account the economic conditions at the time.

He said it was regrettable if the report of Mitsuzuka's comments had given the wrong impression, adding that he hoped remarks made by the finance minister and other ministry officials would be accurately interpreted (by the media).
But the vice minister said that in an overall discussion of the tax system, the idea of raising the weight of indirect taxes would be at the centre of the talks.
